The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $U$ and the prescribed external two-form $F$ be as in [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], and let the translational motion obey the adopted action law [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]. For a $C^1$ spin or polarization vector $s$ along the worldline with $g(s,U)=0$, define $G:=g_s/2$ and $K:=F(s,U)=g(s,F^\sharp(U))$. Adopt the transport law

(a) [Components] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, define the
covariant components of the **electromagnetic two-form** $F$ in the chart by
$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}:=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}:=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$
($i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) and $F_{ab}:=-F_{ba}$, the index-raised components being
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Here
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the spatial permutation symbol of
[[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]. Then $F$ is a $C^k$ type-$(0,2)$
tensor field on $U$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], alternating at every event, and the
components above are exactly its component functions: at $p\in U$ the tensor
$F(p)$ is the bilinear form $F(p)(u,w)=F_{ab}(p)u^aw^b$ on $V$ in the
coordinates $u^a,w^b$ of $u,w$ in $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$. Indeed each $F_{ab}$ is
a finite sum of products of the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ of the chart
coordinates with the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$, hence a $C^k$ function of
$x(p)$, and the component criterion of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] applies.
In the flat specialization, a named inertial chart with $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres uses $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, matching [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]].

For constants $\alpha,a,b\in\mathbb R$, consider the restricted linear transport equations
$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left(aF^\sharp(s)+\frac{b}{c^2}U\,\kappa\right),\qquad \kappa:=g(s,F^\sharp(U)).$$
For every initial $s(\tau_0)$ there is a unique solution on each compact subinterval of $I$. Along any such solution,
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(U,s)=\alpha(1-a-b)\kappa.$$
Consequently, the orthogonality constraint $g(U,s)=0$ is preserved when $a+b=1$, and on that constraint $g(s,s)$ is constant. For $\alpha\ne0$, matching the rest-frame spatial law
$$\frac{d\mathbf s}{d\tau}=\alpha G\,(\mathbf s\times\mathbf B)$$
for all spatial $\mathbf s,\mathbf B$, with $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, forces $a=G$ and $b=1-G$. This uniqueness is only within the displayed two-term ansatz; no uniqueness among all covariant spin-transport laws is asserted. If $\alpha=0$, the rest-frame equation does not identify $a$ or $b$.

Assume the charged test-body quantities and local potential domain of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], the flat-space sign convention of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and the adopted fixed-endpoint action postulate [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], and assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. For a finite $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ in that domain, where $a<b$ are proper-time endpoints, and the local $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variations of the postulate, choose the orientation-preserving parameter $\lambda=\tau$; the segment is stationary for the adopted action if and only if

derivations.claim: In the lemma [F2], set $a=G$ and $b=1-G$. The postulate [A1] has exactly this displayed transport equation because $-(G-1)=1-G$, and [F3] gives the matching translation equation $D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U)$. Thus $a+b=1$ in the lemma; its derivative identity gives $D_\tau g(U,s)=0$. The initial value is zero by [A2], hence orthogonality is preserved.

With $g(U,s)=0$ from step 1.1 and [A2], the same lemma gives $\tfrac12D_\tau g(s,s)=g(s,D_\tau s)=0$: the $F^\sharp$ term vanishes by skew-adjointness, and the term proportional to $U$ vanishes by orthogonality. Thus $g(s,s)$ is constant.

In the general ansatz, [F2] shows that for $\alpha\ne0$, preservation for arbitrary $\kappa$ requires $a+b=1$. In the rest frame, the spatial comparison in [F2] gives $a=G$ when the stipulated target law holds for every spatial $\mathbf s,\mathbf B$; substituting into $a+b=1$ gives $b=1-G$. If $\alpha=0$, both transport equations vanish and impose no coefficient condition. This establishes uniqueness only in the stated ansatz and model.

derivations.claim: If $F=0$, [F7] and the BMT postulate [A1] make both right-hand sides zero, so $D_\tau U=0$ and $D_\tau s=0$. For $G=0$ and general field, the spin equation reduces to $D_\tau s=\alpha U\,g(s,F^\sharp(U))/c^2$. Since [F7] gives $a=\alpha F^\sharp(U)$, this equals $U g(a,s)/c^2$. The full Fermi–Walker expression in the Statement has the additional term $-a g(U,s)/c^2$, which is zero by [A2]; thus the stated branch is exactly Fermi–Walker transport.

Let $\Lambda$ be a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and transform $U,s,F$ as vector and two-form data. Metric preservation [F3] and the defining identity of $F^\sharp$ imply $F'{}^\sharp(\Lambda v)=\Lambda F^\sharp(v)$: pair both sides with an arbitrary $\Lambda w$ and use $F'(\Lambda w,\Lambda v)=F(w,v)$. The scalar $g(s,F^\sharp(U))$ and constraint $g(U,s)=0$ are preserved. Therefore applying $\Lambda$ to each BMT and translation equation gives the same equation for the transformed data.

In the uniform rest magnetic field in [A2], [F7] gives $F^\sharp(U)=0$ because $\mathbf E=0$, so $U=(c,\mathbf0)$ remains at rest and $\kappa=g(s,F^\sharp(U))=0$. The cross-product convention [F1,F2] gives $d\mathbf s/d\tau=\omega\,\mathbf s\times\widehat{\mathbf B}$. Decompose $\mathbf s=\mathbf s_\parallel+\mathbf s_\perp$; the parallel part is constant. Differentiating the displayed sine–cosine formula gives $-\omega\widehat{\mathbf B}\times\mathbf s_\perp=\omega\mathbf s_\perp\times\widehat{\mathbf B}$ at every $\tau$, and at $\tau_0$ it equals the prescribed initial vector. Uniqueness of the linear transport equation in [F2] makes this the exact solution. If $qG=0$ the formula reduces to constant spin.

On the rest slice, put $e=T^{00}$ and $j^i=T^{0i}/c$. Contracting the exact flat moment formula [F6] with $\tfrac12\epsilon_{kij}$ gives $s_*^k=\int\epsilon_{kij}x^ij^j d^3x=\int(x\times j)^k d^3x$. Thus [F4] gives $|\mathbf s_*|\le\ell Mc$; divide by $Mc>0$ for the first inequality. The hypotheses of [F5] are exactly the rest momentum and spin condition in [A2], so every timelike observer shift lies inside the disk of radius $|\mathbf s_*|/(Mc)$ and the boundary is not attained. In the case $\mathbf s_*=0$, [F5] gives only zero shift and [F4] gives the trivial lower bound $\ell\ge0$. In the momentum rest frame, $S^{0i}=0$ and $S^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}s_*^k$, so direct contraction gives $S_{ab}S^{ab}/2=|\mathbf s_*|^2$; together with $M=\sqrt{-p^2}/c$, this shows the radius is a Lorentz scalar. A Lorentz map sends the momentum-rest hyperplane isometrically to the transformed momentum-rest hyperplane, so the support radius $\ell$ is unchanged for the transformed complete rest-frame data. The BMT vector $\mathbf s$ has not entered either estimate; only a separately adopted identification $\mathbf s=\mathbf s_*$ would allow its magnitude to be substituted.

[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] applies.

For any acceleration $a=D_\tau U$ within the Lorentz-force model, the $G=0$ branch is Fermi–Walker transport on the orthogonal spin subspace:
$$D_\tau s=\frac{1}{c^2}\bigl(Ug(a,s)-a g(U,s)\bigr)=\frac{U}{c^2}g(a,s).$$
In an inertial rest frame with uniform $\mathbf E=0$ and constant $\mathbf B\ne0$, $U=(c,\mathbf0)$ is stationary and the $G$ branch has the exact solution
$$\mathbf s(\tau)=\mathbf s_\parallel+\cos(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf s_\perp-\sin(\omega\Delta\tau)\widehat{\mathbf B}\times\mathbf s_\perp,\qquad \omega=\frac{qG}{m}|\mathbf B|,\quad \Delta\tau=\tau-\tau_0,$$
where the projections are parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf B$.

Fix $c>0$ and a future unit observer $n$ in an affine Minkowski spacetime as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. Identify the positive-definite rest space $n^\perp$ with $\mathbb R^3$ and its Euclidean measure $d^3x$. Let $e:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ and $j:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be Lebesgue-integrable, both zero almost everywhere outside $\overline B_\ell(0)$ for some $\ell>0$. Suppose $|j(x)|\le e(x)/c$ almost everywhere. Define
$$E_0:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e(x)\,d^3x>0,\qquad M:=E_0/c^2,\qquad \mathbf s_*:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}x\times j(x)\,d^3x.$$
Then $\mathbf s_*$ is absolutely integrable and
$$|\mathbf s_*|\le\ell Mc,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \ell\ge\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc}.$$
The hypotheses are the full mathematical content of this estimate; it is not a bound for a quantum point particle or for a source whose energy density or momentum density fails them.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space, with signature $(-+++)$, and fix $c>0$. Let $p$ be a future timelike vector with rest-frame components $p=(Mc,\mathbf 0)$ for $M>0$. Let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ satisfy the momentum supplementary condition $S^{ab}p_b=0$, and set $s_*^k:=\tfrac12\epsilon_{kij}S^{ij}$ in an oriented orthonormal rest-space basis. For every future unit observer
$$n=\gamma(1,\mathbf v/c),\qquad \gamma=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2},\qquad |\mathbf v|<c,$$
define
$$\delta^a:=\frac{S^{ab}n_b}{p\cdot n},\qquad S'^{ab}:=S^{ab}-(\delta^ap^b-\delta^bp^a).$$
Then $p\cdot n\ne0$, $\delta\cdot p=\delta\cdot n=0$, and $S'^{ab}n_b=0$. If the representative point changes by $z\mapsto z+\delta$, the total angular momentum $J=z\wedge p+S$ is unchanged by this stipulated spin-shift rule. In the rest space,
$$\boldsymbol\delta=\frac{\mathbf s_*\times\mathbf v}{Mc^2},$$
If $\mathbf s_*\ne0$, the shifts of all future timelike observers fill the open disk in $\mathbf s_*^\perp$ of radius $|\mathbf s_*|/(Mc)$; the boundary is a supremum and is not attained. If $\mathbf s_*=0$, only the zero shift occurs. This is an exact affine-flat algebraic result.

It is distinct from the potential-dependent covector defined in [[lem-rpm-charge-gauge-boundary]].
- The **spin or polarization vector** is a $C^1$ tangent vector field $s(\tau)\in T_{z(\tau)}M$ constrained by $g(s,U)=0$, so it lies in the positive-definite instantaneous rest space $U^\perp$.

derivations.claim: Under [A2], $\widehat{\mathbf B}=\mathbf e_3$, $\mathbf s_\parallel=0$, $\mathbf s_\perp=s_0\mathbf e_1$, and the angular frequency in the rest-spin theorem is $\omega=\alpha G B=qGB/m$. Substitution in that theorem gives the displayed $\mathbf s(\tau)$; differentiating yields $d\mathbf s/d\tau=\omega s_0[-\sin(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf e_1-\cos(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf e_2]$, equal to $\alpha G(\mathbf s\times B\mathbf e_3)$. The initial value at $\tau_0$ is $s_0\mathbf e_1$.

The independent body data [A2] satisfy the hypotheses of [F2]'s size lemma, so $|\mathbf s_*|=S_*$ gives $\ell\ge S_*/(Mc)$. The centroid lemma says the observer shifts fill the open disk in $\mathbf s_*^\perp$ of radius $S_*/(Mc)$; because $\mathbf s_*=S_*\mathbf e_3$, this is exactly the displayed $\mathbf e_1$–$\mathbf e_2$ disk, with every strict interior point attainable and the boundary unattained.

The first calculation uses the polarization $\mathbf s$ and the second uses the body moment $\mathbf s_*$. [F3] imposes no equality between them, so the body-size inequality contains $S_*$ and does not constrain $s_0$ without an extra identification assumption.
